comment_purpose: Git Crafter's own process maps, an instance of the template's library (pages/maps). Every repo keeps its own maps file, separate from every other repo's (the owner, 2026-11-03). A repo's Process page shows only the maps its config names, never these.
comment_format: An entry uses a library map by id ({"use": "delivery"}) and changes only what differs, by step id. Or it is a map of the repo's own, written out in full. A library map takes name, why, ideal, sources, critical_path, time_bar and steps; each step takes name, short, tools, rule, rule_ref, metric, icon, gates, gates_from, or drop: true (pages/library.mjs). A map of its own: id, name, why, steps, and optionally critical_path, time_bar (one metric whose detail rows are its step hours, drawn as one stacked bar), ideal and sources. Each step: id, name, tools, rule, rule_ref (a path under repo_url, or an https link), exactly one metric, and optionally short, icon, gates and gates_from. The metric is an id on this repo's Quality page, rated by that page's goal. Six steps at most (pages/build.mjs MAX_STEPS). pages/maps/README.md has the format.
comment_gates: gates are the rules a step passes through. gates_from adds what each repo's files say: hooks (its git hooks), workflows (its CI workflows) or deploys (its deploy jobs).

maps.why: A change to Git Crafter, from the plan the owner approves to merged on main

tools: App sessions, each in its own worktree
plan.rule: The session where the owner approves the plan orchestrates and starts every session it can foresee in that turn.

tools: Explore agent on Haiku for wide reads
build.rule: Claude builds and reviews; open-weight models do the cheap bulk work.
gates: pre-push runs no tests; CI runs them (site decision 93)

tools: GitHub Actions, standard runners, ubuntu-slim for light jobs
Included Actions usage, 300 USD, a budget that stops at it
Free lanes: Blacksmith and Ubicloud free minutes, public repos
The app's PR monitor with Auto-fix
ci.rule: CI, test suites and builds run on GitHub Actions; the Mac runs only rare, small, quick things.

review.rule: A reviewer runs the checks on the head commit and reports no blocking finding; a fix needs a new review.
gates: A review pinned to the reviewed head SHA, clean or blocking (site decision 95)
Guard test payloads go only to bash_guard.py --check; shell probes run in CI (rules/gates.md)

merge.rule: The orchestrator merges the reviewed head SHA when every check is green; never --auto or --admin.
gates: Merge with the literal reviewed SHA, typed, never read at merge time

maps.why: A merged change to Git Crafter, from the Pages build to live, and back when it fails

tools: pages.yml on every push to main
build.rule: Every merge to main builds and publishes the pages on its own; nobody deploys by hand.

ship.rule: A merged change is live once its push goes green, within minutes.

verify.rule: A publish whose checks fail, or pass only on a rerun, counts as a failed change.

tools: Re-run pages.yml on the last good commit
restore.rule: A failed publish re-runs on the last good commit before anyone debugs it, so main stays red for minutes.

maps.why: Git Crafter's own code, from measured to simplified, deleted, explained, checked and held small
A finding in Git Crafter, from intake to the issue or card a merged pull request closes
